chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj but did not touch the Stone (Hajar al-Aswad) and did not enter the Ka'bah. He said: 'It is from the Sunnah; if he is unable, then Allah is more deserving of making excuses.'
ai.seo_question: Is touching the Stone and entering the Ka'bah obligatory for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between obligatory pillars and recommended acts by confirming that Istilam (touching the Black Stone) and entering the Ka'bah are Sunnah, not Fard. This ruling provides practical flexibility for pilgrims, emphasizing that Allah is more deserving of excuse for any inability to perform these specific recommended acts, thereby alleviating undue burden on the worshipper.
